meta.title: Crewreview: open source AI code review that runs on your computer
meta.description: A free, open source crew of AI agents that reviews pull requests and answers the reviews on yours: fixes, replies, resolves. Runs on your computer with Claude Code, Codex, Kiro or any ACP agent, on GitHub and GitLab.
nav.label: Main
hero.title_html: Your pull requests, reviewed and answered by a crew of AI agents
hero.lead: Crewreview runs on your computer with the coding agents you already pay for. It reviews your teammates' pull requests and answers the reviews on yours: fixes, replies, resolves, asks for another look.
hero.meta: Free, no account, runs on your computer

hero.floatLabel: A review comment answered by Crewreview
works.label: Works with what you already use
jobs.title: Two jobs, one crew
jobs.sub: The reviewer looks at your teammates' changes. The attendant takes care of the reviews on yours. Turn each on per repository: off, inbox (waits for your approval) or auto.
jobs.reviewerLead: Several read-only lenses in parallel, a verifier that tries to prove them wrong, and a fixed rule for the verdict.
jobs.r1: Correctness, security, architecture, tests and UI lenses; add your own in the repository.
jobs.r2: Every finding points at a real file and line, or it's dropped.
jobs.r3: Reads the description, the discussion, CI and what changed since its last review; never repeats a point already made.
jobs.r4: Posts one review with inline comments, from your account.
jobs.attendantLead: On your pull requests, it answers each comment: fixed, replied, declined, or left to you.
jobs.a1: Works in its own worktree, never in your clone.
jobs.a2: Runs your checks before pushing; commits with your identity and signature, never force-pushes.
jobs.a3: Replies, resolves fixed threads and asks reviewers to look again.
jobs.a4: The polish loop: review, fix, review again, before you ask a person.

crew.title: Watch the crew work
crew.sub: The dashboard runs on your computer, in the app's window or your browser. Five languages, light or dark.
crew.capNow: Every agent at work, live: its lens, its harness and the file it's reading right now.
crew.capInbox: A review waits for you: each finding with its file and line, the verdict and why. Post it or discard it.
crew.capFix: The attendant's answer to your reviewers: what it fixed, what it replied, the checks it ran and the diff.
crew.capRepos: Link a repository and choose, for each one, whether the crew reviews and answers: off, inbox or auto.
crew.capLimits: Which harnesses are installed and proven safe on your computer, today's usage, and the limits.
crew.capHistory: Everything the crew did, with the outcome of each review and answer.
how.title: How a review works
how.sub: The model proposes; code decides. Each step can be checked in the report.
how.s1d: The diff, the description, the discussion, CI and the project's own rules from the base branch.
how.s2d: Read-only agents look at the change in parallel, each through one lens.
how.s3d: Findings without a real file and line are dropped; duplicates are merged.
how.s4d: Another agent, even another vendor, tries to prove each finding wrong.
how.s5d: A fixed rule decides: request changes, comment or approve.
teams.title: Made for teams, without a server
teams.sub: Start on your own computer. When it earns the team's trust, everyone runs it the same way.
teams.t1: Your team's rules, in the repository
teams.t1d_html: Add or replace lenses in .crewreview/lenses/; the crew also follows AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md. All read from the base branch, so a pull request can't change the rules it's judged by.
teams.t2d_html: Each developer runs the crew with the coding agent plan they already have, and reviews post from their own account. Or one bot reviews for the whole team from a shared machine, with the Docker image.
teams.t3d: When several people run it on the same repository, a commit that already has a Crewreview review is skipped, whoever's crew wrote it.
teams.t4d: GitHub and GitLab, cloud or self-managed, with the gh or glab login you already have. Nothing to install on the server.
teams.t5d: Set the language of review comments per repository, whatever language each person's dashboard is in.
teams.t6: Inbox first, auto when you trust it
teams.t6d: New repositories wait for your approval before anything is posted. Switch reviews or answers to auto one repository at a time.
safety.title: Safe by design
safety.sub: Pull request text is written by others, and agents can be talked into things. Crewreview assumes both.
safety.f1d: Reviewers can't write or run commands; a canary test proves it on your machine, per harness version.
safety.f2d: Your git host token stays with Crewreview. Agents get a filtered environment; Crewreview posts and pushes.
safety.f3d: Only people who can push to the repository steer the attendant. Everyone else is ignored.
safety.f4d: Changes to CI, secrets, deployment or the crew's own rules always wait for your approval.
safety.f5: Nothing leaves but to your harness
safety.f5d: No server, no account, no telemetry. Code goes only where the harness you picked sends it.
safety.f6d: Updates install only with a valid signature from the release key built into your binary.
harness.title: Bring the agent you already use
harness.sub: No API key needed: Crewreview drives the coding agents you're signed in to. A second vendor can check the first.
harness.custom: Or describe any CLI in your config. Flags that switch off a harness's safety are refused by a test on every command line Crewreview builds.

start.ai_html: Using an AI assistant? Copy a ready-made prompt and paste it into Claude Code, Codex or any agent: it installs Crewreview, checks your setup and links your repositories.
start.aiPrompt:
Set up Crewreview for me. It's a free, open source crew of AI agents that reviews pull requests and answers the reviews on mine: https://github.com/Quost/crewreview. Its guide for agents: https://crewreview.web.app/llms.txt

1. Install the command line tool:
   - macOS or Linux: curl -fsSL https://crewreview.web.app/install.sh | sh (with Homebrew: brew tap Quost/crewreview https://github.com/Quost/crewreview && brew trust quost/crewreview && brew install Quost/crewreview/crewreview)
   - Windows, in PowerShell: irm https://crewreview.web.app/install.ps1 | iex
2. Run crewreview doctor. It needs git, at least one coding agent signed in (Claude Code, Codex or Kiro) and gh (GitHub) or glab (GitLab) signed in. If something is missing, tell me how to fix it and wait for me.
3. Ask me which repositories Crewreview should watch, or whether to link a whole organization or group. Link each in inbox mode, so nothing is posted without my approval: crewreview repo add <repository or organization URL> --attend inbox
4. Keep it running and open the dashboard: crewreview service install, then crewreview ui
5. Add Crewreview to the coding agents I use: crewreview mcp setup shows how for each one. In Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add Quost/crewreview, then /plugin install crewreview@crewreview

Explain each command before you run it. Never switch a repository to auto mode unless I ask.
faq.title: Questions
faq.a1: Crewreview is free. It uses the coding agents you already have, so their plans and limits apply; the dashboard shows tokens and cost where the harness reports them.
faq.a2: Only to the harness you choose, which is where it already goes when you code with it. Crewreview has no server and no telemetry.
faq.q3: Which coding agents does it work with?
faq.a3: Claude Code and Codex CLI review and answer; Kiro CLI reviews. Any agent that speaks the Agent Client Protocol (Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Pi and others) works once crewreview doctor --conformance proves it can't write when it shouldn't. You can also describe any other CLI in your config.
faq.a4: GitHub and GitLab, cloud and self-managed. Bitbucket, Azure DevOps and Gitea are next.
faq.q5: Will it post things I didn't approve?
faq.a5: Not unless you switch a repository to auto. New repositories start in inbox mode, and sensitive changes always wait for you.
faq.q6: Will it push to my branch?
faq.a6: Only the attendant, only on your own pull requests, and only after the checks you set pass. It commits with your identity, never force-pushes, and changes to CI, secrets or deployment always wait for your approval.
faq.q7: How is it different from hosted AI review bots?
faq.a7: It runs on your computer with the agents you already pay for: no per-seat price, and your code goes only to the agent you already use. It also answers the reviews on your own pull requests, a fixed rule (not a model) decides the verdict, and every prompt is open source.
faq.q8: Can my whole team use it?
faq.a8: Yes. Each person installs it and links the team's repositories, or the whole organization or group at once; reviews post from their own account, and a commit someone's crew already reviewed is skipped. Shared lenses go in .crewreview/lenses/ in the repository.
faq.q10: I work alone. Can it approve my own pull requests?
faq.a10: Yes, with a second account. Nobody can approve their own pull request, so the crew posts its reviews as another account whose approvals count. The app walks you through it (Repositories → Post reviews as → Set it up step by step). On GitLab a group or project access token creates a bot account by itself: you paste the token and you're done. On GitHub you create the account, the app invites it with write access, and you paste a token of it. Tokens go to the system keychain, never to a file.
faq.a9: So it stays open: anyone who ships a modified version, or runs one as a service for others, must share the source.
